name: Los Thuthanaka
label: Self-released
lede: Two Aymara siblings, one Bandcamp upload with no warning, and a 61-minute record Pitchfork put ahead of every other album of 2025.

eras.title: E+E and a Virginia sample
eras.text: Before the siblings shared a name, one of them was making collage records as E+E and then as Elysia Crampton, building a catalog out of Southern hip-hop, Andean folk and long stretches of Virginia and Bolivia.

years.src: Vice: Elysia Crampton and the Art of Survival · Wikipedia: Chuquimamani-Condori
years.h: E+E: the first name, and a crowd of collaborators
years.p: Vice's profile says the future Chuquimamani-Condori adopted the moniker E+E in 2008, a handle for mixes, edits and collaborators rather than a solo persona.
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates the E+E name to the early 2000s, while Vice's 2016 interview puts the adoption in 2008. The project was a loose one: contributing writers, DJ mixes made from keyboard, acapellas and a sampler.

Vice also reports the artist grew up in a small town near Monterrey, Mexico, took piano lessons as a child, and spent time in Virginia and La Paz. The artist described that mobility as key to survival.

years.src: Wikipedia: American Drift · Vice: Elysia Crampton and the Art of Survival
years.h: American Drift: Virginia, Bolivia, one long collage
years.p: Elysia Crampton's first album on Blueberry Recordings began in 2012 in Roanoke and Richmond, Virginia, and was finished partly in La Paz. Pitchfork gave it 8.1.
years.xp:
Per Wikipedia, the record draws on crunk and Southern hip-hop, Bolivian and Peruvian prog rock, black spirituals, blues, huayno and cumbia, and ties precolonial Aymara history to African-American history.

Vice reports the artist's grandfather died in late fall 2015 while the record was in its final stretch, and the family's Italian restaurant in Weyers Cave, Virginia is part of the backstory.

years.src: Wikipedia: Elysia Crampton Presents: Demon City · Vice: Elysia Crampton and the Art of Survival
years.p: Released July 22, 2016 on Break World Records, the 25-minute record billed itself as an epic poem, with Why Be and Lexxi alongside Rabit and Amobi.
years.xp:
The second track is titled "After Woman (For Bartolina Sisa)," a nod to the 18th-century Aymara resistance leader. Wikipedia lists a Metacritic aggregate of 88 and a Pitchfork score of 8.2.

Vice reports that the artist's grandmother Flora is one of the record's dedicatees.

eras.title: A new name, unmastered
eras.text: The artist reclaims an Aymara name, puts out records from a museum commission and a Bandcamp page, and the sound gets louder, dirtier and more danceable at once. Meanwhile a younger brother is releasing hours of solo guitar.

years.h: Quirquincho Medicine arrives under the name Chuquimamani-Condori
years.p: Wikipedia lists the July 25, 2019 self-release as the first under the Aymara name given by the artist's mother, replacing Elysia Crampton.

years.h: ORCORARA 2010 on PAN, with proceeds to AIM SoCal
years.p: Commissioned for a 2018 Geneva show, then released digitally May 1, 2020 and on vinyl July 10, mastered by Rashad Becker.
years.xp: XLR8R reports the piece honors Paul Sousa, an incarcerated man who served as a firefighter in California's Sierra Nevada, and that proceeds went to American Indian Movement West and AIM SoCal.

years.h: Joshua Chuquimia Crampton starts a solo run with The Heart's Wash
years.p: His debut is 15 pieces of solo guitar running 96 minutes, written in non-traditional notation, per Wikipedia. 4 (2021) and Profundo Amor (2023) followed.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Crampton was born in 1983 in San Diego and raised partly in rural Mexico, and credits his grandparents with teaching him Andean rhythms. He names two childhood concerts as formative: Los Kjarkas and the Smashing Pumpkins.

years.h: DJ E drops with no label and lands at No. 9
years.p: Pitchfork gave the 29-minute self-release 8.0, and later ranked it No. 9 on its list of the best albums of the 2020s so far.
years.xp: Wikipedia describes it as a densely layered collage of siku panpipes, synths, grand piano and a circular saw, deliberately unmastered as a rejection of "clean" sound. Pitchfork's Sam Goldner called it a binary-smashing collage.

eras.title: The siblings go public
eras.text: Joshua's solo guitar records set up the noise side; then in March 2025 the two release one record under one name, and it becomes the year's consensus pick.

years.cap: Los Thuthanaka, self-released on Bandcamp, March 2025.
years.src: Stereogum: Stream Chuquimamani-Condori · Wikipedia: Los Thuthanaka
years.h: Los Thuthanaka appears on Bandcamp with no warning
years.p: Eight instrumentals, 60:42 in all, credited to Chuquimamani-Condori and Joshua Chuquimia Crampton. Nothing announced it first.
years.xp:
Stereogum's Chris DeVille called it an easy shortlist contender for 2025's best album, pounding and throbbing, and compared the club-plus-live-band setup to Darkside. The artist's statement, quoted by Stereogum, calls the record a milestone with prayers for rain and gratitude.

Wikipedia lists Chuquimamani-Condori on keyboards, sampler, CDJ, ronroco and bombo, and Joshua on guitar, bass and artwork, and says it is dedicated to Chuqi Chinchay, a figure tied to queer guardianship in Aymara belief.

years.h: Huayño, caporal, kullawada, and everything clipped
years.p: Track lengths mostly top eight minutes and are built like continuous DJ mixes, with static and clipping left in on purpose.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, the record rebuilds Andean forms through ronroco, bombo italaque drums, keytar, electric guitars and CDJs. Track titles carry Aymara translations.

years.big: Its best score since Fiona Apple, per Wikipedia
q: Ceremonial but swaggy, cataclysmic but healing, unrefined but magnificent.
years.src: Wikipedia: Los Thuthanaka · Album of the Year
years.p: Pitchfork's Joshua Minsoo Kim called it ceremonial but swaggy; the site then ranked it first in its 50 best albums of 2025.
years.xp: Album of the Year lists Pitchfork's rating as 93 out of 100 for a March 22, 2025 release date. Wikipedia's reception section also lists Paste at No. 2, The Wire at No. 3 and Stereogum at No. 14 on their year-end lists, and says the score was Pitchfork's highest since Fetch the Bolt Cutters (2020).

years.h: On tour: Cafe OTO, the Empty Bottle, Brussels
years.p: The siblings took the record on the road through 2025, with fan-shot sets from London, Chicago and Botanique in Brussels.

years.h: Silver Lion at the Venice Biennale
years.p: Wikipedia reports Chuquimamani-Condori was awarded the Venice Biennale Silver Lion in 2025, and the Biennale programmed a Los Thuthanaka set.
years.xp: The Biennale Musica programme listed both a Los Thuthanaka performance and a separate solo piece, Cry of Our Guardian Star. The Biennale's own award page could not be fetched, so the wording of the citation is not given here.

eras.title: Wak'a and Anata
eras.text: Two more releases in months: a group EP built on Aymara oral history and Joshua's solo record of clipped guitar.

years.h: Joshua's Anata: 25 minutes, all in the red
years.p: Self-released February 4, 2026. Pitchfork gave it 7.6, with Daniel Bromfield calling it some of the most elemental in-the-red music ever recorded.
Released April 3, 2026: three tracks, 18:27, plus a booklet titled The Lake Before the Sun Was Born. Pitchfork gave it 8.0.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, the duo spent years gathering Aymara oral histories from community members and archives for the text. Pitchfork's Sasha Geffen said it commemorates their work to preserve Aymara lore.
